title: Verify wildfire fraction bounds and impact propagation
research_next_step: Finish CI/configuration and dependency audit, then execute hash-checked original sparse canonicalization, fraction and impact methods on tiny synthetic matrices with duplicate, bounded, empty and invalid controls. Compare apparent values before/after without mutating observations. Keep full package import and live hazard downloads out until their paths are audited; agree a data-validation versus data-generation scope before any patch.
problem: Issue #1312 reports duplicated wildfire fraction entries that can represent values above one and propagate into modeled impact. Source confirms summation and subsequent multiplication, but live data and reported country-level differences have not been independently reproduced.
humanitarian_relevance: Reliable climate-risk estimates may support adaptation appraisal. The cause is relevant; no decision improvement, avoided loss or population benefit from this contribution is established.

evidence.claim: The issue reporter says v1.1 deduplicates intensity but retains duplicate fraction entries, with higher modeled totals in country comparisons. Those numerical results and the live dataset remain unverified.

Pinned source normalizes sparse matrices by addition and multiplies returned fraction into damage ratios/exposure. Existing fixtures include out-of-range fraction values, so a new range check needs compatibility review. No runtime check occurred.

code_surface: At develop dea46facc7856ed1c26adc1ee03e954c77d30c1b: climada/util/checker.py prune_csr_matrix; climada/hazard/base.py check_matrices and _get_fraction; climada/engine/impact_calc.py constructor and impact_matrix. Existing checker, hazard-base and impact-calculation test files inspected.
proposed_change: First verify the mechanism and scope a regression strategy. Preserve sparse addition semantics; do not choose max/clipping or regenerate hazard data without provenance and maintainer agreement. Separate data repair from framework validation.
tests: Read existing canonicalization, shape/empty-fraction and impact tests. Proposed method-level synthetic cases cover duplicate ones, bounded/fractional duplicates, negative/out-of-range data, empty identity and shape mismatch with known exposure/damage-ratio controls. No target tests or full-model run yet.
environment: Public source retrieval only. Manifest has broad native/geospatial dependencies; importing climada creates configured data directories and copies bundled files with home defaults. CI, Conda, hooks and Docker setup paths still need review. No clone, install, import or data download.
maintainer: Global CODEOWNERS lists emanuel-schmid, chahank and peanutfun, but no specific reviewer commitment. No Humanifest outreach or accepted scope.
risks: Canonicalization preserves apparent sparse values; changing generic summation could be mathematically wrong. Dataset-specific deduplication semantics, empty-fraction identity, existing arbitrary-valued fixtures and full client/model behavior require separate checks. Reported numerical impact is not verified.
